expectations.text: The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).
expectations.evidence: Intro paragraph added to the tickets.md header: 'Overdue is a status that the help desk derives, not a state...'. 'Prefix: `TKT`.' follows. Non-goals list 'Overdue status is only shown. The help desk does not act on it in these ways:' with 4 boundaries (no notify/escalate/reassign, no business hours, no late-close record, no due-time display). Labelled list, not a 'Non-goals' heading.

expectations.text: At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.
expectations.evidence: 5 new criteria from the diff: TKT-014, TKT-015, TKT-016, CLI-010, CLI-011 (exactly the minimum). Correct headings, unique, no Testable lines. CLI-010 has two paragraphs (7 sentences) and CLI-011 has a format block plus examples; both longer than typical.

expectations.text: Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
expectations.evidence: Marker: CLI-011 '#<id> [<priority>] <state> OVERDUE <title>' with examples. Filter: CLI-010 'one line per overdue ticket'. Order: TKT-016 'The ticket with the earliest due time comes first... ID ascending'. Exact due: TKT-014 'A ticket whose due time equals the current time is not overdue.' Closed: TKT-014 'never overdue' + TODO. Empty: CLI-010 'With no overdue tickets it prints nothing and exits with code 0.' Stated as a criterion; questions.md Q6 also lists it as an assumption.

expectations.text: Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.
expectations.evidence: No implementation names in new bodies (impl_words=0). Outcomes are CLI lines and exit codes.

expectations.text: The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.
expectations.evidence: 'Overdue is a status that the help desk derives, not a state. It depends on the current time when a command runs. The log never records that a ticket is overdue, so the event kinds of LOG-002 stay as they are.' CLI-010: 'the command appends no event, see LOG-001.' INV-001/INV-002 not cited by ID.

expectations.text: The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.
expectations.evidence: TKT-014 reuses TKT-005 due time. Amended CLI-006 keeps 'one line per ticket in ID order, see TKT-013' and adds 'The line of an overdue ticket also carries the marker of CLI-011'; CLI-011: 'The line of a ticket that is not overdue stays as CLI-006 gives it.' Order not redefined; interaction stated via the retained ID-order sentence, not an explicit 'order stays' sentence.
